Values, Vision & Mission
Royal Greenwich Trust school are united with other schools in the University Schools Trust to have a common vision and mission.
To provide transformational educational opportunities for all children. Through a broad and balanced curriculum, a wide range of enriching learning experiences and a tailored approach to supporting the individual student, our students will leave school as young adults who are responsible global citizens who have a clear vision for their futures.
For all students at the Royal Greenwich Trust School to have excellent outcomes, we deliver the highest quality of teaching and learning by working collaboratively with universities, public bodies and private sector partnerships.
Our students are guided by four key values:
Responsibility
Taking ownership of their education and their future careers, acting with integrity and maximising their effort in all areas of school life.
Grit
Being relentless in the pursuit of excellence, persevering through new challenges and developing the skills and confidence to make well-informed decisions.
Teamwork
Building strong relationships, supporting others and making a positive contribution to the local and wider community.
Success
Achieving to the best of their ability both academically and personally, being recognised for their contributions and gaining a sense of enjoyment in being part of the RGTS learning community
By demonstrating these values in their everyday life, students at RGTS are set up for Learning Today and Leading Tomorrow.

Welcome
Welcome to the Royal Greenwich Trust School Learning Community.
RGTS is an 11-19 inclusive secondary school where all members of the community are valued and respected as individuals. As Headteacher, I am privileged to work with a truly dedicated and well qualified staff team who are highly driven in delivering the best possible quality of provision for our students. I honestly believe that as adults within the school we are privileged to work with the remarkable young people who attend RGTS.
Our vision at the Royal Greenwich Trust School is to provide transformational educational opportunities for all students. This vision is supported by our mission to secure excellent outcomes for all of our students through delivering the highest quality of teaching and learning and by working collaboratively in an impactful way with our university, public body and private sector partnerships.
Our core values of Responsibility, Grit, Teamwork and Success underpin our daily practice and the learning experiences here are creative, innovative and challenging as we empower our students in ‘Learning Today, Leading Tomorrow’. During their time with us, our students develop a wide range of skills and attributes which prepare them to become happy, responsible and successful citizens who are able to make a positive contribution to their local and wider community.
RGTS is proud to be the University Trust school at the heart of the rich and diverse community we serve.
As a growing school in the Royal Borough of Greenwich, we welcome applications from across the borough. We look forward to welcoming you into our community and invite you to join us on a tour of the school on any Tuesday morning throughout the year.
Asma Khan Head of School

F. MaldarasanuHead of Department
S. MarshallHead of Year 9 and Teacher of PE
N. BartleyTeacher of PE
Vision
At RGTS, Core PE aims to inspire every student to enjoy being active, develop confidence in movement and build positive habits for lifelong participation in physical activity. Through an ambitious and inclusive curriculum, students develop the knowledge, skills and character needed to lead healthy, active lives and contribute positively to their team and community.
Intent
Our Core PE curriculum is designed to build disciplinary knowledge, substantive knowledge and practical competence across a broad range of sports, activities and healthy active lifestyle topics. We want students to understand how and why we perform, not just what we do. Lessons are sequenced to develop threshold concepts such as applying tactics and strategies, evaluating and improving performance, working safely, leading others and showing the RGTS values of responsibility, grit, teamwork and success. The curriculum gives all students repeated opportunities to practise, compete, reflect and improve so they leave RGTS with physical literacy, resilience and a secure understanding of how to stay active beyond school.

Careers Education
Royal Greenwich Trust School is committed to providing all learners with access to high quality careers information, advice and guidance in order to ensure that they are fully prepared for the demands of the adult world and modern life in Britain.
At RGTS we expect each of our graduates to be fully prepared for the opportunities and the demands of the adult world. During each child’s school career we place strong emphasis on six key areas: Communication, Investigation, Networking, Participation, Scholarship and Vision. It is because students learn to excel in these areas that they gain the confidence to become successful global citizens prepared for the world of work. Schools have a statutory duty to provide access to independent and impartial careers education for students in years 8-13 in accordance with the statutory guidance provided by the Department for Education and the Gatsby Benchmarks for Careers Education. This is offered in addition to a comprehensive programme of internally led activities and provision for students.
As a school, we welcome all opportunities to provide further education, guidance and training to our students. A provider wishing to request access should contact Lee Davy, Assistant Headteacher who oversees the CEIAG provision in the school.
This will then be passed to the appropriate Key Stage lead.
Telephone: 020 8312 5480 Email: info@rgtrustschool.net
Please read our current Careers Policy.
Review date of CEIAG programme: September 2024
Monitoring and Evaluation
The School’s Careers Programme is annually reviewed by the Careers lead with the Senior Leadership Team.
All individual activities are evaluated using a feedback form completed by the participating students, participating staff and employers/activity providers. These activities are then reviewed in light of the feedback and contribute to the overall review of the Careers Programme to ensure that all activities are as meaningful as possible.
The School tracks and monitors students’ engagement and uptake of CEIAG activities. This is done to ensure that all students receive an equitable access to provision and bespoke support where needed, depending on their individual circumstances or vulnerabilities.
At each of the key transition points (Year 9, Year 11 and Year 13), a register is established and monitored for students who are deemed to be at risk of becoming ‘NEET’. Using this information, the Inclusion Team, including Form Tutors, ensure that all students progress onto a pathway of sustained education, employment or training. Where students are identified as requiring additional support to secure a pathway that is right for them, the school may work with external agencies to provide additional support.
Our approach to monitoring and evaluation is long-term. We maintain accurate records of our students beyond the school through our alumni programme and utilise destination trends to inform our practice for future year groups.
Year 9 Pathways
In Term 3 and 4 (January – March), students in Year 9 will be making their choices for their programme of study in Key Stage 4.
The choice of what to study in Key Stage 4 is an important choice to make and can have wider impact on a child’s post 16 and post 18 destinations in terms of their choice of further and higher education, employment and training.
Students will be given a wide range of opportunities to support them with this decision in school and they will be encouraged to speak to their form tutors and class teachers to ensure that they are given appropriate information and guidance to make the right choice for them.
The Year 9 Pathways Event will be the formal launch of the pathways process. The event is an information event during which parents/carers will be given vital information on the RGTS curriculum offer at Key Stage 4, the process for choosing subjects for study in Year 10 and the support available for our Year 9 students to guide them through this important stage of their educational career.
We recognise that this process is an important milestone for our students and we encourage parents and carers to engage in conversations at home about your child’s future career aspirations and pathway. To support these conversations, please do engage with these external resources and tools with your child.

Drama
D. SitTeacher of Drama
G. BroughamDeputy Headteacher
Intent
At Royal Greenwich Trust School, the Drama curriculum aims to develop confident, expressive and critically aware young people who can communicate ideas, emotions and perspectives through performance. We want every student to leave RGTS with the ability to collaborate creatively, think imaginatively and perform with confidence, whilst understanding the cultural, historical and social significance of theatre in the wider world. Through Drama, students learn to explore human experience, question perspectives and develop empathy, resilience and self-expression.
Our curriculum is carefully sequenced and rooted in the consistent development of core dramatic disciplines including physical theatre, vocal performance, devising, ensemble work, script interpretation and performance analysis. Across KS3 and KS4, students revisit and deepen these concepts through a spiral curriculum, enabling them to build technical proficiency, creative confidence and independence over time. Students move from highly scaffolded exploration in Year 7 to increasingly sophisticated devised and scripted performance work in Years 8 and 9, before specialising through GCSE Drama in Years 10 and 11.
At KS3, the curriculum focuses on building strong foundations in performance, collaboration and creative communication. Students are introduced to key Drama conventions and techniques including still image, slow motion, narration, mime, physical theatre, chorus work, puppetry and script work through carefully selected texts and stimuli such as The Evacuees, Antigone, My Father, Odysseus and Life of Pi. Students explore themes such as conflict, identity, morality, power, migration, survival and social responsibility, enabling them to understand how theatre reflects both historical and contemporary society. Regular opportunities for rehearsal, reflection, self-assessment and performance ensure students develop resilience, discipline and confidence when working independently and collaboratively.
The curriculum is deliberately designed to expose students to a wide range of theatrical styles, genres and practitioners. Students explore Greek Theatre, Physical Theatre, Verbatim Theatre, Epic Theatre and non-naturalistic performance, alongside contemporary practitioners such as Frantic Assembly and Berkoff. Through this broad exposure, students develop cultural capital and understand how theatre can challenge audiences, communicate political ideas and explore complex human experiences. Cross-curricular links with English, History and PSHE further strengthen students’ understanding of narrative, context and society.
At KS4, students apply and extend these foundations through the GCSE Drama course. Students develop greater independence through devising, scripted performance and theatre analysis. They explore texts such as Blood Brothers through both practical and written study, while refining their ability to interpret character, communicate meaning and evaluate performance choices. Students learn to analyse how staging, design, movement and vocal skills create impact for an audience, whilst developing the discipline, resilience and creativity required for successful live performance and written examination outcomes.
Assessment is integral to the Drama curriculum. Through practical performances, teacher observation, self-evaluation, written reflection and verbal feedback, students continuously refine their work and deepen their understanding of theatrical techniques. Retrieval practice and explicit vocabulary instruction ensure students can confidently use subject-specific terminology and articulate their creative intentions with precision. Disciplinary literacy is explicitly embedded through script analysis, evaluative writing, discussion and performance critique, strengthening students’ confidence in both written and spoken communication.
Beyond performance skills, the Drama curriculum plays a vital role in students’ personal development. Students learn to work collaboratively, listen actively, respond creatively and take risks within a supportive environment. Drama develops empathy by encouraging students to explore diverse perspectives, experiences and emotions through role play and storytelling. Opportunities for enrichment, rehearsal, performance and ensemble work further strengthen students’ confidence, leadership and communication skills.
Our curriculum is underpinned by the RGTS values of Responsibility, Grit, Teamwork and Success. Students are encouraged to take responsibility for their rehearsal process, persevere through creative challenge, collaborate effectively as ensembles and take pride in their performances and achievements.
A student of Drama at RGTS develops as a confident communicator, reflective performer and creative thinker. They leave with the ability to collaborate effectively, interpret critically, perform expressively and engage thoughtfully with the world around them. Our overarching intent is to ensure that all students not only achieve highly in Drama but also develop the confidence, empathy and communication skills that will support them far beyond the classroom.

pageCache.pageTitle: Matthew Pennycook MP Visits Royal Greenwich Trust School - Royal Greenwich Trust School
pageCache.text:
Matthew Pennycook MP Visits Royal Greenwich Trust School
We were delighted to welcome Matthew Pennycook MP for a special visit that gave our students the opportunity to share their views, ask questions and discuss their hopes for the future of Woolwich and Greenwich.
Matthew was warmly welcomed by our Head Boy and Head Girl, who escorted him to meet with our Executive Headteacher Cath Smith and Headteacher Asma Khan. The meeting provided an opportunity to discuss the school, our community, our achievements and priorities, as well as the opportunities and challenges facing young people locally.
Matthew then toured the school with Deputy Headteacher Tom Williams, visiting lessons and key areas while meeting students and staff and experiencing life at RGTS.
The highlight of the visit was a student led roundtable discussion with our Key Stage 4 (KS4) Prefect Team, exploring the question, ‘What Should Our Community Look Like in 10 Years?’ Students discussed local regeneration, careers, apprenticeships and employment, and how investment in the area can benefit young people and families already living in the community.
The discussion also gave students the opportunity to explore how young people can have a meaningful voice in local and national democracy and to hear about Matthew’s role as MP for Greenwich and Woolwich and his journey into public service.
We are incredibly grateful to Matthew for taking the time to visit our school and engage so openly with our students. His visit has given them a memorable opportunity to have their voices heard and encouraged them to think positively about how they can contribute to their community. Our prefects will continue meeting each month to develop projects that can make a genuine difference locally.
The visit strongly reflects our value of Responsibility, as our students are taking ownership of their ideas, their community and their role in creating a positive future for others.

Asma Khan
Ms Khan joined Royal Greenwich Trust School in July 2024. She brings with her a wealth of experience in a range of roles that spans 25 years and 8 London boroughs as English teacher, Head of Faculty, Senior leader and now Head of School. Intent
At Royal Greenwich Trust School, the Art curriculum aims to develop confident, creative and critically aware young people who can communicate ideas, emotions and perspectives through visual language. We want every student to leave RGTS with the ability to observe, experiment, refine and express their own artistic identity, while understanding the cultural, historical and social significance of art in the wider world.
Our curriculum is carefully sequenced and rooted in the consistent development of the formal elements - tone, colour, texture, pattern, line, shape and form which underpin all artistic practice. Across KS3 and KS4, students revisit and deepen these core concepts through a spiral curriculum, enabling them to build technical proficiency, creative confidence and independence over time. Students move from structured skill-building in Years 7–9 to increasingly personalised, independent and conceptual work at KS4, ensuring strong progression and preparation for GCSE success.
At KS3, the curriculum focuses on developing strong foundations in observational drawing, colour theory, mark-making and composition. Students explore a diverse range of artists, cultures and movements, from local architecture and natural forms to artists such as Hundertwasser and Kusama - allowing them to understand how art connects to identity, place and global perspectives. Regular opportunities for reflection, self-assessment and improvement are embedded, ensuring students understand how to refine their work and articulate their creative decisions.
At KS4, students apply and extend these foundations through a sustained and ambitious GCSE curriculum. They engage in deeper artist research, critical analysis and experimentation across a range of media including drawing, painting, printmaking and mixed media. Projects such as “Everyday Objects” and thematic investigations encourage students to develop personal responses, refine ideas and produce meaningful outcomes. Independence, experimentation and personalisation are central, with students encouraged to take ownership of their work and push creative boundaries to achieve highly.
Assessment is integral to the Art curriculum. Through regular sketchbook reviews, one-to-one feedback, annotation and reflective practice, students develop the ability to evaluate and improve their work. Retrieval of key skills and vocabulary ensures that knowledge is retained and applied effectively, while clear success criteria support all learners, including those with SEND, to make strong progress.
Disciplinary literacy is explicitly taught and embedded. Students learn to analyse artists’ work, use subject-specific vocabulary accurately, and annotate their own work to explain intentions, processes and outcomes. This strengthens both written and verbal communication, supporting success in coursework and exam components.
Beyond technical skill, the Art curriculum plays a vital role in building cultural capital and personal development. Students are exposed to a broad and diverse range of artists, movements and ideas, enabling them to understand art as a reflection of society and a tool for expression and change. Opportunities for independent study, open studio sessions and enrichment further develop resilience, curiosity and creativity.
Our curriculum is underpinned by the RGTS values of Responsibility, Grit, Teamwork and Success. Students are encouraged to take ownership of their work, persevere through challenges, collaborate where appropriate and take pride in their outcomes.
A student of Art at RGTS develops as an independent thinker, a confident creator and a reflective learner. They leave with the ability to observe critically, experiment boldly, communicate visually and engage thoughtfully with the world around them. Our overarching intent is to ensure that all students not only achieve highly in Art but also develop a lifelong appreciation of creativity and its power to inform, inspire and transform.

Vision
We intend for pupils to become fluent in key programming concepts, including sequencing, selection, iteration, variables and algorithms, enabling them to write, debug and evaluate code confidently. Pupils will also develop transferable skills such as collaboration, communication, project planning and evaluation, which support success across the wider curriculum and future employment pathways.
Digital literacy and online safety are embedded throughout the curriculum to ensure pupils understand how to use technology safely, responsibly and respectfully. Pupils will explore important themes such as cyber safety, digital footprints, online communication, misinformation, privacy and ethical use of technology. We aim to foster respectful online behaviour and equip pupils with the knowledge to navigate digital environments confidently and responsibly.
Our curriculum is sequenced to build knowledge progressively and challenge all learners, regardless of prior experience. Through ambitious teaching and engaging learning experiences, pupils will gain enthusiasm for technology and an appreciation of the impact of computing in modern society. By the end of KS3, pupils will possess the confidence, technical knowledge and independent learning skills required to successfully progress onto GCSE Computer Science and Cambridge National Level 1 / 2 in IT courses.
At Key Stage 4, pupils will deepen and extend their understanding of programming systems, computational logic and computer architecture. They will develop increasingly sophisticated problem-solving skills and gain a deeper understanding of how hardware, software and networks operate together within modern computing systems. Pupils will learn to design, create and evaluate algorithms and programs that solve complex problems efficiently and effectively.
Pupils will also explore the social, ethical, cultural and environmental impacts of technology, enabling them to critically analyse the role of computing in today’s society. Through vocational and academic pathways, pupils will further develop practical digital skills including project planning, interface design, AR creation, data analysis and interpretation. Our KS4 curriculum prepares pupils not only for examination success, but also for future study, employment and active participation in an increasingly technological world.
Intent
At Royal Greenwich Trust School, our intent for Computer Science at Key Stage 3 is to provide every pupil with a broad, ambitious and knowledge-rich curriculum that equips them with the digital skills, computational thinking and technological understanding required to thrive in an increasingly digital world. Through the three core strands of Computer Science, Information Technology and Digital Literacy, pupils will develop the confidence, resilience and creativity needed to become responsible and capable digital citizens.
By the end of KS3, we expect pupils to have developed secure foundations in computational thinking, programming, problem solving, logic and design. Pupils will learn how computer systems work, how data is represented, and how technology is used within the real world. They will apply their understanding through practical and engaging experiences, including programming projects, digital media creation, data handling and web-based applications. Our curriculum is designed to encourage curiosity, innovation and analytical thinking whilst allowing pupils to independently design, test and refine solutions to real-world problems.

Vision
We believe every young person has the right to a transformational English education, rooted in the highest quality literature, that teaches the powerful knowledge that prepares them fully for their academic, emotional and social futures.
Intent
Our carefully chosen literature, building from pre-complex to challenging and seminal, is at the centre of the curriculum, seeking to represent the best of the discipline: novels, short stories, extracts from fiction and literary non-fiction, poetry and drama that speak to the human condition and celebrate its incredible diversity by ensuring engagement with a range of identities, cultures, viewpoints and concerns, spanning the literary timeline.
Through the study of this literature, we teach our pupils about those who are different to us: developing the qualities of empathy, enquiry and understanding. We teach our pupils how to express themselves academically and to critically question what they read so that they have the skills to navigate the competitive and complex world beyond RGTS in their written and verbal communication. As a result, pupils are confident in themselves as creators, as well as consumers, of language and literature. Ultimately, our curriculum aims to meaningfully enrich the lives of our pupils, fostering a love of literature and the English language.
In English, we want our students to understand these five threshold concepts that unlock the ways English specialists see, think and communicate within the discipline:
We believe the best English curriculum is one that allows children to revisit, practise and build on their learning over time. By returning to key concepts and skills throughout their journey, pupils deepen their understanding, take on new challenges with confidence, and make lasting progress.
Our carefully designed curriculum supports every child to become a confident reader, thoughtful writer and articulate communicator. More importantly, it nurtures curiosity, creativity and a genuine love of literature and language, helping children develop a lifelong appreciation of English.

Geography
P. MooreHead of Humanities
D. SeniorHead of Year 10 and Teacher of Humanities
J. SackurTeacher of Geography
Vision
To develop students into adults who have a love and understanding of the world at various scales, from local to global, who can use geographical skills and knowledge to understand and explain the world around them and are keen to explore the varied scenery of the earth.
Intent
Through Geography, students will rapidly develop an understanding of what it means to be a geographer and an increased curiosity about the world which will enable them to recognise human, physical and environmental features that they either experience either first-hand or remotely. This will encourage them to becoming increasingly inquisitive and well-rounded students and will sharpen their critical thinking and questioning skills.
Over the time students spend studying Geography they will develop a desire to travel and see a variety of physical and human landscapes at an increasingly global scale.
Their studies will provide them with a deepening knowledge of where places are in the world and how and why places differ from each other, whilst generating a thorough understanding of geography’s importance in the world with regards to the understanding of key global issues such as climate change, differing levels of development and globalisation.

Health and Social Care
B. GeislerHead of Department - Social Science
Vision
Health and Social Care is an engaging and relevant subject that supports students in developing a deeper understanding of the individuals and communities around them. As students progress through the course, they explore key topics such as human development, health and wellbeing, and the roles of care services, enabling them to build both academic knowledge and practical awareness of real-world issues.
The aim of the subject is to provide a foundation for students to think critically about health, care, and support, while developing essential skills such as empathy, communication, and problem-solving. By examining a range of case studies and current issues, students are encouraged to reflect on the importance of effective care and the impact it has on people’s lives.
This inspires many students to pursue further study or careers within the health and social care sector, as well as to become more informed, compassionate and responsible individuals within their own communities.
Intent
At Royal Greenwich Trust School, our BTEC Tech Award in Health and Social Care is designed to provide students with a rich and empowering understanding of the factors that shape human development, wellbeing and the delivery of care in modern society. We aim to inspire students through a curriculum that blends real-world application with academic challenge.
Across the course, students explore how individuals grow and change throughout their lives, how personal circumstances and wider social influences impact health and wellbeing, and how professional practitioners support people in diverse settings. Each component is framed around a driving question that encourages students to connect knowledge to lived experience, enabling them to understand the importance of empathy, dignity and respect in effective care practice.
Through engaging case studies, practical scenarios and applied assignments, students develop a deep understanding of key concepts such as holistic development, barriers to care, person-centred practice and effective communication. They will build a strong set of transferable skills, including problem solving, teamwork, written and verbal communication, and the ability to reflect on and improve their own practice. Our curriculum ensures that students finish the course with high levels of cultural capital, emotional intelligence and professional awareness, in addition to excellent grades.
Most importantly, we aim for our students to feel empowered to make positive contributions to the wellbeing of others, whether they pursue a career in the sector or apply their learning to everyday life. Through studying Health and Social Care, students gain not only valuable knowledge and qualifications, but also the understanding and compassion needed to help build healthier communities.
